title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Ten documented Purdue traditions, from fountain runs and campus superstitions to songs, cheers and the annual kart race.

cards.title: Run the fountains
cards.subtitle: Engineering Fountain, Loeb Fountain and Stone Lions Fountains
cards.notes: During Boiler Gold Rush, follow the orientation route through the named fountains; treat this as a warm-weather campus walk and follow event guidance.
cards.short_summary: A Boiler Gold Rush rite of passage centered on Purdue’s fountains.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences calls running through the fountains a rite of passage and a key part of Boiler Gold Rush.
cards.access_notes: The source describes this as part of Boiler Gold Rush orientation; participate only through the organized program.

cards.title: Avoid walking beneath the Bell Tower
cards.subtitle: Purdue Bell Tower
cards.notes: Notice how this campus superstition shapes routes around the tower; it is folklore, not a graduation rule or academic requirement.
cards.short_summary: A modern Purdue superstition links the Bell Tower passageway with four-year graduation.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences documents the rumor that walking under the Bell Tower means not graduating within four years.
cards.access_notes: The university identifies this as a rumor/superstition, not an official policy.

cards.title: Seek the lionheads’ exam luck
cards.subtitle: Stone Lions Fountains, outside Stanley Coulter Hall
cards.notes: Find the four lion heads outside Stanley Coulter Hall and read the finals-week folklore; rely on preparation rather than any promised result.
cards.short_summary: A four-lion drinking-fountain superstition tied to final exams.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences says students believe drinking from all four lion heads will grant all A’s on final exams.
cards.access_notes: The university presents this as a superstition; the Stone Lions Fountains are outside Stanley Coulter Hall.

cards.title: Mark the first snow at Slayter Hill
cards.subtitle: Slayter Hill
cards.notes: When snow arrives, view the hill’s long-running sledding tradition from a safe distance or use appropriate sledding equipment and conditions.
cards.short_summary: First snowfall turns Slayter Hill into a memorable Purdue gathering point.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences states that Slayter Hill fills with students sledding on the day of the first snow.
cards.access_notes: Winter conditions vary; do not use improvised equipment or obstruct others.

cards.title: Catch Thrill on the Hill
cards.subtitle: Slayter Hill before football games
cards.notes: Check the football-weekend schedule, then hear the All-American Marching Band’s pre-game concert from Slayter Hill.
cards.short_summary: The marching band’s pre-game Slayter Hill concert anchors football Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences identifies Thrill on the Hill as the Purdue All-American Marching Band’s pre-game concert at Slayter Hill.
cards.access_notes: Occurs during football season; consult current Purdue event information for timing.

cards.title: Remember the towering Homecoming displays
cards.subtitle: Historic residence-hall front-yard displays
cards.notes: Use this as a piece of Purdue history: explore archival images and Homecoming context rather than looking for an active display competition.
cards.short_summary: A former residence-hall display competition that shaped Purdue Homecoming memories.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue University Residences says the Homecoming display competition was launched in 1976 and discontinued in 1992.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued tradition: the display competition ended in 1992; Purdue still holds Homecoming events.

cards.title: Follow the Grand Prix
cards.subtitle: Purdue Grand Prix kart race
cards.notes: Watch for annual race information and learn how student teams prepare for the 160-lap competition and its associated campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories describes Grand Prix as a Purdue tradition in which 33 drivers and teams compete in a 160-lap race.
cards.access_notes: Annual event; consult current Grand Prix Foundation information for participation and spectator details.

cards.title: Ride the Boilermaker Special
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s official locomotive-style mascot
cards.notes: Look for official campus opportunities to ride the Boilermaker Special; the experience is documented as a student rite of passage.
cards.short_summary: A ride aboard Purdue’s official mascot has become a student milestone.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories calls riding the Boilermaker Special, Purdue’s official mascot, a rite of passage for students.
cards.source_title: Purdue’s can’t-miss traditions for new Boilermakers
cards.access_notes: Rides depend on official availability and event operations; do not assume public access at a given time.

cards.title: Join in “Hail Purdue”
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s official fight song
cards.notes: Learn the chorus before a game or gathering, then join the song when it is led by Purdue’s bands or musical organizations.
cards.short_summary: Purdue’s fight song has been sung and clapped along with for more than a century.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue Stories states that “Hail Purdue” was adopted as Purdue’s official fight song and is sung at University functions.
cards.source_title: Boilermakers have played and sung ‘Hail Purdue’ across the globe — and even in space
cards.access_notes: A campus song tradition; performance timing depends on the event.

cards.title: Answer with “Boiler Up!”
cards.subtitle: Purdue’s rallying cry
cards.notes: Recognize the call in its game-day and campus context; Purdue’s style guide notes that fans use it as a greeting and in the fight song.
cards.short_summary: A 1997 football-era phrase that became Purdue’s ubiquitous rallying cry.
cards.evidence_claim: Purdue states that Arnette Tiller introduced “Boiler Up” in 1997, fans greet one another with it, and it was incorporated into “Hail Purdue.”
cards.source_title: Purdue Brand Studio Editorial Style Guide
cards.access_notes: Use is informal and appropriate across Purdue events and digital campus communication.
